nodes.name: Sunlight
nodes.desc: Light reaching the forest floor limits growth beneath the dense summer canopy, so many understory plants rely on gaps and clearings.

nodes.name: Caspian moisture and rain
nodes.desc: The Alborz range catches moist air from the Caspian Sea, giving the northern slopes far more rain than the dry country to the south.

nodes.name: Forest soil and leaf litter
nodes.desc: Fallen leaves and wood build a damp organic soil that holds water and nutrients for the trees.

nodes.name: Fungi and bacteria
nodes.desc: Break down leaf litter, dead wood and carcasses, returning nutrients to the soil.

nodes.name: Oriental beech
nodes.desc: The dominant tree of the Hyrcanian forest, especially in the middle mountain zone, and a source of beechnuts in autumn.

nodes.name: Chestnut-leaved oak
nodes.desc: A common broad-leaved tree of the lower forest, producing acorns eaten by many animals.

nodes.name: European hornbeam
nodes.desc: A widespread broad-leaved tree of the Hyrcanian forests, often growing with beech and oak.

nodes.name: Bracken
nodes.desc: A fern of forest clearings and edges that spreads across open ground.

nodes.name: Wild oats and grasses
nodes.desc: Grasses of clearings, forest edges and farmland, recorded in large numbers near the forest.

nodes.name: Social vole
nodes.desc: A small rodent of open grassy ground that feeds on plants and is prey for many predators.

nodes.name: Great tit
nodes.desc: A small woodland bird that eats insects and, in autumn and winter, seeds such as beechnuts.

nodes.name: European roe deer
nodes.desc: A small deer that browses leaves, buds and herbs at forest edges and in clearings.

nodes.name: Wild boar
nodes.desc: An omnivore that roots in the forest floor for nuts, roots, plants and small animals.

nodes.name: Caspian red deer
nodes.desc: A large deer that eats grasses and leaves. The leopard is its main predator, and wolves and bears take fewer.

nodes.name: European pine marten
nodes.desc: A forest-dwelling hunter of small mammals and birds, recorded near the Hyrcanian forests.

nodes.name: Wildcat
nodes.desc: A small forest cat that hunts rodents, birds and reptiles.

nodes.name: Common buzzard
nodes.desc: The most recorded raptor in the area. It hunts voles and other small prey from perches and in flight.

nodes.name: Golden jackal
nodes.desc: An opportunist that hunts small animals and also scavenges carcasses.

nodes.name: Common raven
nodes.desc: A scavenging crow that feeds on carrion and other food.

nodes.name: Persian leopard
nodes.desc: The top predator of the Alborz forests, which are among its most important habitats in Iran. It hunts deer and wild boar.

nodes.name: Gray wolf
nodes.desc: A pack hunter that takes deer and other prey across the region.

nodes.name: Brown bear
nodes.desc: An omnivore that eats nuts and plants and sometimes takes deer.
